_doc: Approval-gate (K22) rules for implementing-cloudformation-from-spec, read by core/gate/spec-approval-gate.py. Each setting carries a why; each command rule carries examples that the gate's unit tests execute. Rule ids carry the cloudformation- prefix because the plugin merges every skill's rules and keeps one rule per id. A rule whose decision is write decides nothing itself: its writes object names what the matched command writes as a side effect (paths relative to the directory it works in, directory_options, file_options, path_options, operands), and the gate judges that like any other write, so it is denied inside the project before approval.
writable_why: Before approval only the plan, its ledger and planning notes may change. .claude/ holds tooling, not product.
approval_why: The skill asks the user to reply 'approve'. Looser words such as 'ok' or 'go' also answer unrelated questions and would unlock edits by accident.

command_rules.why: With AWS::LanguageExtensions, --use-previous-template reuses the processed template with the old literal parameter values, so new parameter values are silently not applied (transform-aws-languageextensions.html, Considerations).
command_rules.message: --use-previous-template keeps old resolved parameter values on LanguageExtensions templates. Submit the original template instead.

match: aws cloudformation create-change-set --stack-name s --change-set-name c --use-previous-template --parameters ParameterKey=K,ParameterValue=v
no_match: aws cloudformation create-change-set --stack-name s --change-set-name c --template-url https://b.s3.amazonaws.com/t.yaml

command_rules.why: Creating, updating, executing or deleting stacks and change sets touches live accounts; create-change-set creates a change set resource in the account. The skill stops at validated templates; the operator or the pipeline deploys, and a dev change set is created only when the user asks for it.
command_rules.message: this changes CloudFormation state in an account. The skill never deploys; approve only if you asked for this exact call.

match: aws cloudformation create-change-set --stack-name s --change-set-name c --template-body file://infra/a.yaml

command_rules.why: These deploy to an account outside the project's pipeline; a TaskCat test run creates real stacks.
command_rules.message: this deploys to an account outside the pipeline. Approve only if you asked for it.

command_rules.why: Planning and verification are read-only. A mutating AWS call from the model bypasses the pipeline and drifts the stacks.
command_rules.message: this AWS CLI call can change live resources outside CloudFormation. Approve only if you intend it.

match: aws iam put-role-policy --role-name r --policy-name p --policy-document file://p.json

command_rules.why: Validation tools are installed by the user's choice: a missing tool is reported, never installed silently, and a failed install never gets a substitute package.
command_rules.message: this installs software. Approve only if you want this exact package installed.

command_rules.why: aws cloudformation package writes the packaged template to --output-template-file ("The path to the file where the command writes the output AWS CloudFormation template", AWS CLI reference). Before approval only ai-planning/ and .claude/ may change, and planning is read-only, so the gate counts it as a write inside the project at the directory the command works in. The upload itself asks under cloudformation-operator-deploys.
command_rules.message: this writes the packaged template into the project. Package after the plan is approved, or write the output outside the project.

match: aws cloudformation package --template-file infra/a.yaml --s3-bucket b --output-template-file infra/packaged.yaml
